evidence: Eight fictional author-labeled procedures in one bounded workflow

cases.procedure: A rush order jumps ahead of a regular order. If packing of the regular order has begun, finish that order before taking the rush one.
Work rush jobs ahead of regular jobs. A regular job's packing begins at label printing. Once that packing begins, complete the regular job before switching.
Serve the urgent carton before the standard carton. Once work on packing the standard carton is under way, complete that carton first.
Give an incoming express job first turn over a regular job. The regular job enters packing when its first item goes into the carton. From then on, finish that job before switching.
Move an express order to the front. Keep a standard order at the station through completion if its packing has started.
Process urgent orders first. Finish a standard order first instead if its packing is already in progress. Printing its label puts the standard order into packing.
Put rush work at the head of the queue. Complete any regular order whose packing has already started before taking up the rush work.
Select the rush order before the ordinary order. Finish packing an ordinary order once packing has begun. Label preparation is preliminary; packing begins when the first item is placed in the carton.
